chapter_seo_title: RMJI Chapter 593: Stone Talismans Explained, Netherworld Lore, and the Nascent Soul’s Notes
chapter_meta_description: Han Li explores a mana-sealed Netherworld village, learning about stone talismans, Yin Beast cores, and the legacy of a Nascent Soul cultivator who died there.
og_title: Stone Talismans and the Beast Core Economy
og_description: In a world without mana, even a Nascent Soul cultivator can die of old age. Han Li learns the rules of survival in the Netherworld Domain.
twitter_title: No mana? No problem. Han Li finds new toys.
twitter_description: Han Li discovers a mana-sealed village with a grim economy of beast cores and a dead Nascent Soul’s notes.

lore_anchors.definition: A cursed, mana-sealed realm where normal spiritual energy is replaced by Netherworld force, accessible only through special techniques and beast cores.
A dark, death-aligned energy substitute in the Netherworld Domain, usable for limited spellcasting through hybrid talisman-formation devices.
A creature born of concentrated Netherworld force; killing them yields rare Yin Beast cores with varying probability.
A rare resource found in the heads of Yin Beasts; used as fuel for defensive spells and protective formations in the Netherworld Domain.
An ancient, partially lost form of talisman carved into stone, modified with formation features to draw on Netherworld force instead of standard spiritual energy.
A cultivator from the Five Dragons Sea living in the Netherworld Domain village, knowledgeable about local customs and the stone talisman system.
A sea region in the cultivation world where the lost art of stone and jade talisman crafting is still preserved.
A catastrophic phenomenon that seals all mana in an area, trapping even high-level cultivators and leaving them vulnerable to the ghost mist.
A weak type of Yin Beast; killing one can rarely yield a small Yin Beast core.
A large, four-eyed ape-like Yin Beast mentioned as a threat to the village.
